A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLATE research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression, MNIST, text classification, LLM adaptation, and computational-efficiency experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds component ablations, geometry diagnostics, compression tests, and four-task sequential results.

M1.justification: The core BAQ^T adapter, weight-derived B/Q construction, and training of A remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 and Algorithm 2 add a sequential extension that merges each trained adapter into the backbone and recomputes B and Q before the next task.

E1.justification: The original datasets and domains remain covered. Appendix C.6 adds a distinct four-task MNIST scenario, 2-versus-3 through 8-versus-9, extending evaluation beyond the original two five-class tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds O-LoRA and L2-Init to the retained MNIST, text classification, and synthetic regression comparisons. O-LoRA also appears in the Middle English comparison, where unsuccessful L2-Init evaluations are reported in prose. These substantially broaden v1's comparisons against LoRA and full fine-tuning.

E3.justification: Added protocols include matched-capacity B/Q controls, predictive KL on old-task inputs, activation-subspace alignment measurements, 20%/30% SliceGPT compression, and four-stage sequential evaluation. The original architecture and training-setting tables remain essentially unchanged; the new analyses introduce substantial additional evaluation designs.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices A.6 and C.3-C.6 add component ablations, Hessian/Gauss-Newton diagnostics, weight-versus-activation alignment, compression robustness, and sequential retention analyses. These directly investigate the proposed mechanism and its boundaries. The original curvature perturbation experiment and hyperparameter sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: The original ten-run mean/standard-deviation protocol is retained. v2 additionally specifies five seeds for the matched-capacity MNIST ablations and reports boxplots and medians over 1,890 curvature probes collected across seeds and batches. These disclosures concern new analyses, not an increase in the original run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, ablation, and robustness outcomes. Newly reported MNIST controls have predictive KL of 0.009 for PLATE versus 0.076-0.113 when Q is replaced; the four-task experiment reports Task-1 accuracy declining from 97.3% to 90.9%. Existing MNIST curves also change between v1 Figure 8 and v2 Figure 5, while several other original figures retain identical results.

T1.justification: The central invariance and forgetting bounds and their proofs are retained. v2 adds a leading-order predictive-KL-to-drift argument in Section 5.3 and mathematical definitions/properties for activation-subspace overlap in Appendix C.4, including its random-subspace expectation. The added curvature diagnostic is empirical rather than a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: a weight-only adapter, drift/curvature-based motivation, controllable plasticity, and improved retention while preserving learning. The revised conclusion and additional experiments elaborate these claims without materially redefining their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Q as the dominant retention mechanism and B primarily as allocating plasticity, refining v1's emphasis on both restrictions reducing drift. Appendix E adds substantive qualifications about residual curvature, imperfect weight-activation alignment, compression, and applicability to short task streams. Several new interpretations nevertheless conflict with the accompanying figures or method description.

D1.justification: v2 documents control construction, predictive-KL computation, compression configurations, and the sequential merge/recompute procedure. Most existing construction details, computational analysis, configuration tables, and code-access information are retained or relocated. The hyperparameter tables still do not supply grids for the newly evaluated baselines.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kumar et al. on L2-Init and Ashkboos et al. on SliceGPT, and removes the Morcos et al. representational-similarity reference. Wang et al.'s orthogonal-subspace work was already cited in v1. The central positioning as weight-only continual PEFT remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: B/Q construction and computational analysis move into Appendix B, several experiments move into Appendix C, and discussion and conclusion are merged. A main-text mechanism section and dedicated limitations appendix are added, alongside condensation and rewriting of experimental discussion.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Comparison plots are redrawn with additional baselines, and new diagnostic figures and an alignment table are added. Several original graphics are retained but relocated, including v1 Figures 2, 6, and 3 becoming v2 Figures 11, 17, and 18.

improvement.justification: Matched-capacity controls, broader baselines, and explicit limitations make v2 more informative and better support assessment of PLATE's mechanism. However, new inconsistencies limit the gain: Appendix C.1 claims less forgetting than L2-Init although Figure 10 shows the opposite over most task distances, and C.4 identifies Q with top singular directions despite B.2's bottom-eigenspace construction. The empirical assessment improves, but parts of its interpretation require correction.
